title: CARDIO-ALPHA: Phase III Trial of Cardivex in Stage 1-2 Hypertension
meta: Cardivex (fictional ACE inhibitor), 10 mg once daily
sections: Background
Cardivex is a fictional long-acting angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor. CARDIO-ALPHA evaluated its antihypertensive efficacy and tolerability against placebo over 12 weeks.
Cohort and methods

A total of 842 adults (mean age 58.4 years, 46% female) with stage 1-2 essential hypertension were randomized 1:1 to Cardivex 10 mg (n=421) or placebo (n=421) at 37 fictional sites. The primary endpoint was the change in mean seated systolic blood pressure (SBP) from baseline to week 12.
Results

Mean SBP decreased by 14.2 mmHg with Cardivex versus 6.1 mmHg with placebo (difference -8.1 mmHg; 95% CI -9.6 to -6.6; p<0.001). Diastolic blood pressure decreased by 8.3 mmHg versus 3.2 mmHg. Blood pressure control (<140/90 mmHg) at week 12 was achieved in 61.5% versus 33.8% of patients.
Safety

The most common adverse event was dry cough (7.3% vs 1.9%). Hyperkalemia (serum potassium >5.5 mmol/L) occurred in 1.8% vs 0.5%. Two cases of angioedema (0.5%) were reported with Cardivex and none with placebo. Discontinuation due to adverse events was 3.1% vs 1.4%.
Conclusion
Cardivex 10 mg produced a clinically meaningful SBP reduction with an adverse-event profile typical of the ACE inhibitor class.

title: Cardivex Post-Marketing Safety Surveillance Report, Year 1
meta: Cardivex (fictional ACE inhibitor), 5 mg and 10 mg tablets
sections: Scope

This periodic safety report summarizes spontaneous and registry-based adverse event reports for Cardivex during its first year of fictional marketing. Estimated exposure was 58,300 patient-years across 41,900 treated patients.
Key findings

Hyperkalemia was reported in 2.1% of registry patients, higher than the 1.8% observed in the CARDIO-ALPHA trial; most cases occurred in patients with eGFR below 45 mL/min/1.73 m2 or concomitant potassium-sparing diuretics. Angioedema incidence was 0.4% (176 cases), of which 12 required emergency airway management. Dry cough leading to discontinuation was reported in 2.6% of patients.
Signal assessment
No new safety signal was identified. The angioedema rate is consistent with the trial estimate. The hyperkalemia signal is considered expected and is linked to renal impairment.
Risk minimization
The label was updated to recommend serum potassium and creatinine monitoring 2 to 4 weeks after initiation in patients with chronic kidney disease stage 3 or higher.

title: GLUCO-BETA: Phase II Dose-Finding Trial of Glucoren in Type 2 Diabetes
meta: Glucoren (fictional SGLT2 inhibitor), 5 mg and 15 mg
sections: Background
Glucoren is a fictional sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitor intended as add-on therapy to metformin.
Cohort and methods

312 adults with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled on metformin (baseline HbA1c 8.2%) were randomized to Glucoren 5 mg (n=104), Glucoren 15 mg (n=104) or placebo (n=104) for 24 weeks. The primary endpoint was the change in HbA1c at week 24.
Results

HbA1c decreased by 0.6% with Glucoren 5 mg, 0.9% with Glucoren 15 mg and 0.2% with placebo. Body weight decreased by 2.4 kg with the 15 mg dose. Fasting plasma glucose decreased by 1.7 mmol/L with 15 mg. The 15 mg dose was selected for Phase III development.
Safety
Genital mycotic infections occurred in 3.8% (15 mg), 2.9% (5 mg) and 1.0% (placebo). Urinary tract infections were reported in 4.8%, 4.8% and 3.8%. No diabetic ketoacidosis was observed.

title: Renal Outcomes with Glucoren plus Cardivex in Diabetic Hypertensive Patients
meta: Glucoren 15 mg + Cardivex 10 mg vs Cardivex 10 mg alone
sections: Objective

To compare kidney function trajectories in patients with type 2 diabetes and hypertension treated with Cardivex plus Glucoren versus Cardivex alone, using a fictional multicenter observational registry.
Cohort

1,204 patients were followed for 24 months: 598 on combination therapy and 606 on Cardivex monotherapy. Mean baseline eGFR was 68 mL/min/1.73 m2 and median urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) was 54 mg/g.
Outcomes

Mean annual eGFR decline was 1.9 mL/min/1.73 m2 with the combination versus 3.4 mL/min/1.73 m2 with Cardivex alone. UACR fell by 31% versus 12%. The composite renal endpoint (40% eGFR decline, dialysis or renal death) occurred in 4.2% versus 7.9% of patients (adjusted hazard ratio 0.54; 95% CI 0.34 to 0.86).
Safety
Hyperkalemia was less frequent with the combination (1.5% vs 2.6%). Volume depletion events were more frequent (2.2% vs 0.8%).
Limitations
Observational design; residual confounding cannot be excluded.

title: Neurolix Adverse Event Review: Pooled Analysis of Migraine Prevention Studies
meta: Neurolix (fictional CGRP receptor antagonist), 60 mg oral daily
sections: Scope
Pooled safety data from three fictional 12-week migraine prevention studies (NLX-201, NLX-301, NLX-302) including 560 Neurolix-treated and 548 placebo-treated adults with episodic migraine.
Most common adverse events

Nausea was the most frequent adverse event (11.0% vs 4.7% placebo), followed by dizziness (6.2% vs 3.1%), constipation (5.4% vs 1.8%) and fatigue (4.1% vs 3.3%). Most events were mild and resolved within two weeks.
Serious adverse events

Serious adverse events occurred in 1.3% of Neurolix patients and 1.1% of placebo patients. Discontinuation due to adverse events was 4.6% vs 2.0%. ALT elevation of grade 3 or higher was observed in 0.3% of Neurolix patients.
Conclusion
Neurolix was generally well tolerated; gastrointestinal events were the main tolerability concern.

title: CARDIO-ALPHA Renal Laboratory Substudy: Potassium and Creatinine
sections: Purpose
To characterize serum potassium and creatinine changes in a laboratory substudy of 214 CARDIO-ALPHA participants (108 Cardivex, 106 placebo).
Methods

Samples were collected at baseline, week 2, week 6 and week 12. Potassium was measured by indirect ion-selective electrode and creatinine by enzymatic assay; eGFR was calculated with the CKD-EPI 2021 equation.
Results

Mean serum potassium increased by 0.21 mmol/L with Cardivex versus 0.03 mmol/L with placebo at week 12. Mean serum creatinine increased by 6.2 umol/L (about 7%) at week 2 and stabilized thereafter. Three Cardivex patients (2.8%) had potassium above 5.5 mmol/L; all had baseline eGFR below 60 mL/min/1.73 m2.
Interpretation
The early creatinine rise is consistent with the expected hemodynamic effect of ACE inhibition and was not progressive.

title: RESP-GAMMA: Phase III Trial of Inhaled Pulmavir for Adult RSV Infection
meta: Pulmavir (fictional inhaled antiviral), 20 mg twice daily for 5 days
sections: Background
Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes significant morbidity in older adults. Pulmavir is a fictional inhaled fusion inhibitor.
Cohort and methods

1,020 adults aged 50 years or older with laboratory-confirmed RSV infection and symptom onset within 72 hours were randomized 1:1 to Pulmavir or placebo. The primary endpoint was time to sustained symptom resolution.
Results

Median time to symptom resolution was 5.1 days with Pulmavir versus 7.4 days with placebo (hazard ratio 1.38; p<0.001). Viral load at day 3 was reduced by 1.2 log10 copies/mL more than placebo. Hospitalization within 28 days occurred in 2.4% vs 4.9% of patients.
Safety
Bronchospasm occurred in 1.6% vs 0.6%, and dysgeusia (taste disturbance) in 3.5% vs 0.4%. No deaths were attributed to study drug.

title: ONCO-DELTA: Phase II Trial of Onkatinib in EGFR-Mutant NSCLC
meta: Onkatinib (fictional tyrosine kinase inhibitor), 150 mg daily
sections: Background
Onkatinib is a fictional third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor for previously treated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
Cohort and methods

Single-arm study of 128 patients with EGFR-mutant advanced NSCLC who progressed after one prior TKI. Median age was 63 years; 22% had stable brain metastases. The primary endpoint was objective response rate (ORR) by RECIST 1.1.
Results

ORR was 38% (49/128; 95% CI 30 to 47). Median duration of response was 8.3 months. Median progression-free survival (PFS) was 9.6 months and the disease control rate was 81%. Intracranial ORR among patients with brain metastases was 32%.
Safety
Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 27% of patients, including rash (8%), diarrhea (6%) and ALT elevation (4.2%). Dose reductions were needed in 19% of patients.

title: Cross-Product Hepatic Safety Signal Review: Onkatinib and Neurolix
sections: Purpose
To review drug-induced liver injury (DILI) signals for two fictional products in the Northbridge portfolio using trial data and spontaneous reports.
Liver enzyme findings

Grade 3 or higher ALT elevation occurred in 4.2% of Onkatinib-treated patients in ONCO-DELTA versus 0.3% of Neurolix-treated patients in the pooled migraine studies. Median time to onset was 6 weeks for Onkatinib and could not be estimated for Neurolix due to few events.
Hy's law cases
One potential Hy's law case (ALT above 3x ULN with bilirubin above 2x ULN) was identified with Onkatinib; none were identified with Neurolix.
Recommendation
Liver function tests every 2 weeks for the first 3 months of Onkatinib therapy are recommended. No additional hepatic monitoring is recommended for Neurolix.

title: Real-World Outcomes of Neurolix versus Triptan-Only Care in Episodic Migraine
meta: Neurolix 60 mg daily prevention vs acute triptan therapy only
sections: Design

Retrospective fictional cohort study using electronic health records from 14 headache clinics. 1,860 adults with 4 to 14 monthly migraine days were included: 742 started Neurolix and 1,118 continued triptan-only care.
Outcomes

At 6 months, monthly migraine days decreased by 4.8 with Neurolix versus 3.1 with triptan-only care. A 50% or greater responder rate was achieved by 47% versus 29% of patients. Acute medication use decreased by 3.9 versus 1.2 days per month.
Persistence and tolerability
Treatment persistence at 6 months was 72%. The most common reason for stopping Neurolix was nausea (5.1% of patients), consistent with the pooled adverse event review.
Conclusion
Neurolix was associated with better migraine outcomes than triptan-only care in routine practice.

title: GLUCO-BETA-EXT: 52-Week Phase III Extension of Glucoren 15 mg
meta: Glucoren (fictional SGLT2 inhibitor), 15 mg once daily
sections: Background
Following the GLUCO-BETA Phase II results, this fictional Phase III study assessed long-term efficacy and safety of Glucoren 15 mg added to metformin.
Cohort and methods
640 adults with type 2 diabetes (baseline HbA1c 8.1%) were randomized 1:1 to Glucoren 15 mg or placebo for 52 weeks.
Results
HbA1c decreased by 1.1% with Glucoren versus 0.3% with placebo at week 52. Body weight decreased by 3.1 kg versus 0.5 kg. Systolic blood pressure decreased by 4.6 mmHg versus 1.2 mmHg.
Safety
Genital mycotic infections occurred in 4.5% versus 1.3%. Diabetic ketoacidosis was reported in one Glucoren patient (0.3%). Discontinuation due to adverse events was 3.4% versus 2.5%.

title: Onkatinib Therapeutic Drug Monitoring: Plasma Trough Concentrations
meta: LC-MS/MS, lower limit of quantification 2 ng/mL
sections: Purpose
To describe steady-state plasma trough concentrations (Ctrough) of Onkatinib 150 mg and their relationship with toxicity in 96 ONCO-DELTA patients.
Results

Median Ctrough at day 15 was 212 ng/mL (interquartile range 158 to 279). Patients with Ctrough above 300 ng/mL had a higher incidence of grade 3 or higher rash (21% vs 5%) and ALT elevation (11% vs 2%). Ctrough was not associated with objective response.
Recommendation
A target trough range of 150 to 300 ng/mL is proposed. Dose reduction to 100 mg may be considered when Ctrough exceeds 300 ng/mL with grade 2 or higher toxicity.

title: IRON-ORBIT: NBX-101 in Adults with Anemia

Cohort and methods

240 adults aged 18 to 75 were randomized equally to NBX-101 or placebo. Treatment lasted 24 weeks. The primary endpoint was hemoglobin change from baseline, except response proportions which were measured at the endpoint visit. Outcome assessors were blinded.
Primary result

At week 24, hemoglobin change was +1.8 g/dL with NBX-101 and +0.7 g/dL with placebo. These values are the prespecified primary analysis of the randomized population. No pediatric results were collected.
Safety
Nausea occurred in 8.3% versus 4.2%; discontinuation due to adverse events was 2.5% versus 1.7%.
Interpretation and limits

The results describe this synthetic 24-week adult study only. Long-term effects, pregnancy outcomes, approved dosing and outcomes in children are not established by this document. No treatment or prescribing recommendation is made.

title: IRON-ORBIT Follow-up: NBX-101 at Week 48
sections: Scope
This fictional extension enrolled 96 selected completers of the IRON-ORBIT study. All extension participants received NBX-101; there was no concurrent placebo arm. Data and participants are invented.
Follow-up result

At week 48, the reported hemoglobin result was +1.5 g/dL. Changes refer to the original baseline; response proportions refer to the follow-up visit. This result belongs to the selected extension cohort, not the original randomized population.
Safety follow-up

Four participants discontinued because of adverse events and two were lost to follow-up. No new safety category was identified in this small fictional cohort; that observation does not establish long-term safety.
Comparison limits

The parent trial and extension differ in follow-up duration and participant selection. The extension cannot support a new placebo-adjusted treatment difference. Use the separate IRON-ORBIT randomized report for the original comparator results.
Missing information
This report provides no pediatric dosing, approval status, pregnancy data or individualized treatment instructions. All findings are demonstration data, not clinical guidance.
